record_reviews.summary: Holland’s 10 December letter follows a visit from Darwin and sets out objections to Origin for possible use in later editions. He asks for a tighter definition of natural selection, distinguishes necessity, accident, instinct and volition, questions whether the theory explains complex organs and instincts, and presses examples including the ear bones, Eustachian tube, eye, electrical and poisonous animals, spider silk and blood corpuscles. He invokes Newton’s Query 31 and his own Mental Physiology. The source is an incoming post-publication critique, dated by the visit; no surviving Darwin response is in this packet.
